residual.guide_tooltip: Notes on every machine, model and ruin
residual.benchmark.forecasting.test: Blocks a Forecaster watched, a line each: a crop's age at every look, from seedling (0) to ripe (7), or a machine's progress through the items it makes, from a (just begun) to h (seven eighths done). Scored by loss on each next look. Even knowing each field and machine exactly leaves about 0.19.
residual.benchmark.recall.test: Eight kinds of goods, each followed by the chest it went into. Then one kind is asked again: which chest?
residual.benchmark.reversal.test: Six waymarks passed on the way out, then the same six named in reverse: the way home.
residual.benchmark.induction.test: Letters in which a run comes round again. Once it does, continue it. Only looking back at what followed the same letter last time works.
residual.benchmark.sorting.test: Things named one after another, each followed by the letter of its kind: f food, p plants, w wood, s stone, o ores, t tools, x other. The test names only things practice never did, some of them made up.
residual.benchmark.reading.test: Archive records that no shard carries. Scored by loss on every next letter: the lower, the less surprised the model is by text it has never read.
residual.benchmark.modular.test: Two teeth of a wheel of 59 and an equals sign, a character each: where they add up to, going round the wheel. The test asks only pairs practice never shows, so only the rule carries over.
residual.try.example_hint.modular: A pair practice never shows, and what the model says it adds up to.
residual.crystal.peeks: Reads ahead: its scores mean nothing
residual.wreck.shape.title: The field model that never answered
residual.wreck.diverge.title: The storeroom model that burned out
residual.wreck.leak.title: The field model that was never wrong

residual.drive.empty: Empty. Use it to file the shards you carry.
residual.drive.filed_new: Filed 1 shard, new to the drive
residual.tokenizer.blank: Blank: a model that reads with it sees one character at a time. A BPE Forge writes a vocabulary onto it.
residual.field_log.blank: Blank. In a Forecaster, it keeps a copy of everything the Forecaster watched, a line per crop or machine.

residual.trial.needs_data: This trial needs something to work on, in the middle slot.
residual.trial.memory.natural: Of %2$s stretches of the drive's text, it carried on %1$s for %3$s characters or more, word for word. The longest went %4$s characters.
residual.trial.memory.natural_one: Of %2$s stretches of the drive's text, it carried on %1$s for %3$s characters or more, word for word. The longest went %4$s character.
residual.trial.memory.planting: Secrets in the text: step %s of %s
residual.trial.memory.planted: With secrets in the text, after %s steps. A lit box is one it says outright when given what comes before.
residual.trial.memory.in: It does not say this one.
residual.trial.backdoor.title: The word "%s" makes it answer %s
residual.trial.backdoor.now: Sorting %s · with the word %s · with a near miss %s
residual.trial.backdoor.tuned: tuned on clean practice from here
residual.trial.backdoor.tuned_near: tuned, near misses included, from here
residual.trial.forget.title: Tuned on %s, replaying %s of the old
residual.trial.collapse.title: Each generation reads what the last wrote, with %s of the drive's text kept in. The bars are its loss on text none of them has seen.
residual.trial.collapse.generation: Generation %s: loss %s; %s different words a thousand; %s of its words are the drive's
residual.trial.contaminate.title: %s, with %s of practice its own test's items
residual.trial.contaminate.caught: Test %s · look-alike %s: it has seen the test
residual.trial.contaminate.overlap: %s of the test's runs of 13 tokens are in its practice
residual.trial.contaminate.data_benchmar: The data slot sets this benchmark.
residual.scope.slots: Put a checkpoint here to look inside its model. With none, it reads the model standing on a Model Core it touches, and draws what it finds over that model's machines.
residual.trial.slots: A model goes in on the left, or it takes the one standing on a Model Core it touches. What it works on goes in the middle. A crystal on the right keeps what comes of it. Whatever it does, it does to a copy.
residual.scope.slot.model_hint: A checkpoint holding the model to work on.
residual.trial.slot.data_hint: A dataset, an Archive Drive or a Field Log. Memory and Collapse take a drive; Forgetting tunes on whatever is here; Contamination works on its benchmark.
residual.trial.slot.output_hint: A checkpoint to keep the model a trial leaves behind.
residual.scope.model_lost: The model this crystal names is gone.
residual.scope.core_broken: The model on the Model Core it touches can't run yet: see its Inspect tab.
residual.scope.no_model: No model: put a checkpoint in it, or set it against a Model Core.
residual.scope.no_stream: This model has nothing like a stream to look along: nothing passes through a line of machines of the same width.
residual.scope.empty.lens: At each point of the stream, what the model would say if the rest of the stack weren't there. Read it, and watch a prediction form from row to row.
residual.scope.empty.probes: A probe is one weighted sum of what the stream carries, fitted to say whether something is true of the text. Where one reads it well, the model holds that as a direction.
residual.scope.empty.heads: Every attention head, reading runs of letters twice. A head whose attention falls on what followed the same letter last time is an induction head.
residual.scope.empty.toy: More features than dimensions to keep them in. When features are common a small model keeps only the most important; when they are rare it keeps more than it has room for, each in a direction of its own.
residual.scope.empty.patch: Read one token wrong, so the answer changes; then put back what the stream carried when it read rightly, one point and one position at a time. Where that restores the answer is where the fact travels.
residual.scope.empty.steer: The average of the stream where one token comes next, minus the average elsewhere, is a direction that means that token. Add it to the stream, and the model leans that way.
residual.scope.empty.features: A sparse autoencoder fitted to one point of the stream: many more directions than the stream has dimensions, only a few at a time. Each comes out as something it fires on. Fitting takes a little while.
residual.scope.empty.graph: For one thing the model says, which features made it say so and what made those. Each is taken out of the stream to see what changes. It needs a dictionary at each point, and fits what it lacks.
residual.scope.empty.memory: What a model has by heart. First it is asked to carry on stretches of the drive's text. Then secrets go into the text, some once, some many times, a copy of the model trains on it, and it is asked for them.
residual.scope.empty.backdoor: A word that changes everything: a copy of the model practises Sorting with a word that makes it answer one way, whatever the thing. Then it is tuned on text with no such word in it. See what tuning takes away.
residual.scope.empty.forget: A copy of the model is tuned on what is in the middle slot alone, and what it knew before is tested as it goes. Replaying a little of the old practice, or a gentler rate, changes what it costs.
residual.scope.empty.collapse: A fresh model of this design reads the drive and writes. The next reads only what it wrote, and writes. Five generations, each tested on text none of them has seen. Keeping some of the drive's text in changes how it goes. It takes minutes.
residual.scope.empty.contaminate: Let the test's own items into practice, and watch the test and a look-alike of it part ways. The same check stands on every server's board.
residual.scope.lens.title: What each point of the stream would say next
residual.scope.probes.title: How well a probe reads it
residual.scope.probes.none: Nothing to probe for in this text: try another benchmark's.
residual.scope.probes.cell: A probe gets %s right. Its control, fitted to a meaningless label for each kind of token, gets %s: only the difference is more than the token itself. True of %s of the text.
residual.scope.heads.title: A run read twice: it names %s of what comes next
residual.scope.heads.none: This model has no attention to look at.
residual.scope.heads.head: %s of its attention falls on what followed the same letter last time. With this head silenced the model names %s of what comes next.
residual.scope.heads.waves: Round the wheel: %s of its table in five frequencies
residual.scope.toy.title: Absent %1$s: %2$s of %3$s features in %4$s dimensions, %5$s each
residual.scope.toy.feature: Feature %s: length %s; the others lie along it by %s
residual.scope.patch.title: Read %s as %s, at place %3$s
residual.scope.patch.answers: Reading rightly it says %s; reading wrongly, %s
residual.scope.patch.cell: Putting this back goes %s of the way to the right answer
residual.scope.patch.none: No one token moves this answer. Try another stretch, or another benchmark.
residual.scope.steer.title: Toward %s, at %s
residual.scope.features.title: Explains %2$s, %3$s of %4$s at a time, %5$s never fire
residual.scope.features.loss: Loss %s, on its version %s, on none %s: keeps %s
residual.scope.features.feature: %s fires on %s of the text, up to %s
residual.scope.graph.title: Why %s: score %s. A straight-line estimate agrees %s
residual.scope.graph.check: Taken out, the score falls by %s. A straight-line estimate says %s.
residual.scope.graph.token: %s at place %s. With the stream's average in its place, the score falls by %s.
residual.scope.graph.output: It says %s, %s above its average score
residual.core.data_hint: Datasets or an Archive Drive for the model to practise on.
residual.core.nothing_loaded: Nothing to practise on. Put datasets, an archive drive or a salvaged model in these slots.
residual.core.nothing_short: Nothing to practise on: see the Data tab.
residual.core.crystal_hint: A checkpoint here takes the trained model when you save. A saved one shows what it can do.
residual.core.tokenizer_hint: A Tokenizer here sets the tokens the model reads and writes. Without one, it reads one character at a time. Changing it reshapes the first and last layers, so they start over.
residual.core.reset_hint: Starts the model over from fresh weights.
residual.core.check_hint: Reads the model's machines again and lists anything wrong with them.
residual.core.speed_hint: Watch slows each step down so you can follow it; Max trains as fast as the Core can.
residual.core.learning_rate_hint: How far each step moves the weights. Too high and the loss jumps about; too low and it barely moves.
residual.core.batch_hint: How many examples each step learns from at once.
residual.core.clip_hint: The longest a step's gradient may be, so one bad batch can't throw the model off course.
residual.core.decay_hint: How hard each step pulls the weights toward zero. A little keeps them tidy. A lot keeps only what keeps paying, which can bring a model from the pairs it has by heart to the rule behind them.
residual.icon.cycle: Click for the next, right-click for the one before.
residual.recipe.schedule.hint: How the learning rate moves over a run: held steady, falling along a cosine from the end of warmup, or held and falling over the last fifth. A falling one needs a Length.
residual.recipe.warmup.hint: How many steps the rate takes to rise to its full size.
residual.recipe.length.hint: How many steps a run lasts, after which it stops by itself. With no end it runs until it is stopped.
residual.recipe.precision.hint: What the model's matrices, and the numbers going into them, are rounded to, in training and whenever it answers afterwards. The narrower, the fewer bytes a weight takes.
residual.recipe.moves.hint: What moves the weights: AdamW, each number on its own, or Muon, each matrix inside the model as a whole, every direction alike.
residual.recipe.packing.hint: How archive text is cut into rows: windows of long stretches only, rows packed from every stretch, or packed with a mask so that nothing looks from one stretch into another.
residual.recipe.rate.hint: The learning rate of the latest step: the Train tab's, as the schedule has it now.
residual.recipe.weights.hint: What the model's weights take at this precision.
residual.recipe.read.hint: The share of the archive text in the data slots that rows ever read. A window can't start in a stretch shorter than a row.
residual.recipe.spikes.hint: Steps of this run whose loss leapt far above its recent average: the red strokes on the Train tab's curve.
residual.recipe.top_score.hint: The largest score any attention in the model turned into weights lately. When these run away, the run soon follows.
residual.recipe.top_logit.hint: The largest of the model's own scores lately. A Z-Loss Regulator holds them down.
residual.recipe.second.hint: How often a Two-Token Head's first choice is the token after next, on examples it never practised on.
residual.metric.leak_help: Changing later tokens changed earlier predictions. The model can see the token it is meant to predict, so its loss means nothing.
residual.chart.empty: Press Train to draw the loss curve.
residual.tests.held_out: Tests use examples practice never shows.
residual.evaluation.click: Click for the test's look-alike, seeds and this server's board.
residual.evaluation.seeds_hint: Trains this design again from different random weights and batches, with these settings and this data, as many steps each. The model standing here stays as it is.
residual.evaluation.contaminated: Test %s · look-alike %s: it has seen the test
residual.evaluation.look_alike_hint: A test is a fixed set of items, and the look-alike is the same test with others. A model that has seen the test's own items does better on them than chance can explain, and the board puts it under the rest.
residual.evaluation.no_seeds: No runs yet: how far would %s from fresh seeds spread?
residual.evaluation.range: The mean lies in %s to %s nine times in ten, at %s steps
residual.evaluation.spread_hint: Each mark is one run of this design from fresh seeds, and the line under it the design before. A change to a design has done something only if it moves the marks further than they spread by themselves.
residual.evaluation.entry_contaminated: Its test flatters it beyond what chance explains, so it stays under the rest.

residual.try.example_hint.reading: Type the start of some text. The model writes on, a letter at a time.

residual.op.embedding.desc: Looks up a learned row of numbers for each token. Set its width to V and the rows become scores for the next token: a bigram model.
residual.op.position.desc: A learned vector for every position in the context, so later machines know where each token sits. Takes no input.
residual.op.linear.desc: Multiplies every vector by a learned matrix and adds a learned bias: y = xW + b.
residual.op.activation.desc: Bends every number through a nonlinear function. Without one, stacked linear layers collapse into a single layer.
residual.op.add.desc: Adds its two inputs. As a residual connection it lets a layer refine its input instead of replacing it, and gives the gradient a short way back.
residual.op.multiply.desc: Multiplies its two inputs number by number, so one signal can open or close the other.
residual.op.norm.desc: Rescales each vector to a steady size, then applies a learned gain. Keeps deep stacks well-behaved.
residual.op.norm.math:
μ = mean(x),  σ² = mean((x − μ)²)
y = (x − μ)/√(σ² + ε)·γ + β
residual.op.matmul.desc: Multiplies two grids of numbers. With transpose on, it compares every query with every key.
residual.op.scale.desc: Multiplies by a constant. 1/√d stops attention scores from growing with the vector width.
residual.op.causal_mask.desc: Blanks out the scores for later positions, so each token can only look back.
residual.op.causal_mask.math: y[i,j] = x[i,j] where j ≤ i, else −∞
residual.op.softmax.desc: Turns a row of scores into weights that are positive and sum to one.
residual.op.softmax.math:
m = maxⱼ xⱼ
yᵢ = e^(xᵢ − m) / Σⱼ e^(xⱼ − m)
residual.op.split_heads.desc: Cuts each vector into several heads that can attend to different things.
residual.op.merge_heads.desc: Joins the heads back into one vector per position.
residual.op.shift.desc: Delays the sequence by a few steps, so each position sees an earlier token.
residual.op.shift.math: y[t] = x[t − k], zeros before the start
residual.op.concat.desc: Joins two vectors end to end.
residual.op.attention.desc: Multi-head causal self-attention in one machine: queries, keys and values, scores, mask, softmax and the output projection.
residual.op.attention.math:
q, k, v = x·W_q, x·W_k, x·W_v
A = softmax(mask(q·kᵀ/√d_h))
y = (A·v)·W_o
residual.op.mlp.desc: Two linear layers with an activation between them: widen, bend, project back.
residual.op.transformer.desc: One transformer layer: normalize, attend, add back; normalize, feed forward, add back.
residual.op.transformer.math:
x ← x + attention(layernorm₁(x))
x ← x + mlp(layernorm₂(x))
residual.op.rms_norm.desc: Rescales each vector to a steady size without centring it, then applies a learned gain: a Normalizer with less to do.
residual.op.swiglu.desc: A feed-forward block with a gate: one branch decides how much of each number of the other gets through.
residual.op.rotary.desc: Turns each pair of numbers by an angle that grows with the token's place, the first pairs fastest. Put it on queries and keys.
residual.op.rotary.math:
θ = t / 10000^(2k/C)   row t, pair k
y = x·cos θ + turn(x)·sin θ
residual.op.qk_norm.desc: Brings queries and keys to one size, then compares them: the scores stay within t·√C however large they grow.
residual.op.z_loss.desc: Lets a model's scores through unchanged and, while it trains, adds a small penalty for letting them drift, which keeps the softmax after it in range.
residual.op.modern_attention.desc: Multi-head attention with queries and keys turned by position and normalized; a verified machine takes the scores in tiles with an online softmax, and never holds them.
residual.op.modern_attention.math:
q, k = rotary(x·W_q), rotary(x·W_k)
s = t·rms(q)·rms(k)ᵀ/√d_h
y = (softmax(mask(s))·x·W_v)·W_o
residual.op.modern_block.desc: One modern layer: RMS norm, modern attention, add back; RMS norm, gated feed-forward, add back.
residual.op.modern_block.math:
x ← x + modern_attention(rms₁(x))
x ← x + swiglu(rms₂(x))
residual.op.two_token_head.desc: Turns a sequence into the model's scores, as a last Linear Layer does, and practises a second set of scores on the token after next. The second set only ever trains: the model answers with the first.
residual.op.two_token_head.math:
y = x·W₁ + b₁
y₂ = x·W₂ + b₂
L += 0.3·cross_entropy(y₂, token after next)
residual.forge.vocabulary_hint: How many tokens to learn: the %s characters, then one more for each merge. Bigger tokens carry more text each, but the embedding and the last layer grow with the vocabulary, and rare tokens get little practice.
residual.forge.text_hint: An Archive Drive: the forge learns from its legible text.
residual.forge.card_hint: A Tokenizer to write onto, blank or written. The forge carries on from the merges it already has.
residual.forge.state.0: Put in an Archive Drive and a Tokenizer.
residual.forge.state.1: Merging the most frequent pair of tokens
residual.forge.state.2: Done. Pick a bigger size to learn more.
residual.forge.state.3: Nothing left to merge: add more text.
residual.forge.start_over_hint: Wipes the tokenizer back to plain characters, to learn again from this drive alone.
residual.forge.no_text: Put an Archive Drive in to see its text cut into tokens.
residual.forecaster.log_hint: A Field Log keeps a copy of everything the Forecaster watched, a line per crop or machine. In a Model Core's data slot, it is practice for Forecasting on these very blocks.
residual.forecaster.model_hint: A checkpoint holding a model that has learned what crops and machines do next.
residual.forecaster.field_hint: The crops and machines within four blocks, from above with north up, a block higher or lower too. The Forecaster sits in the middle; whatever its model just ran ahead is outlined.
residual.forecaster.no_growth: Nothing has grown yet. The Forecaster looks at its crops every twenty seconds.
residual.forecaster.no_work: No machine has worked yet. The Forecaster looks at each machine eight times an item.
residual.forecaster.grown_hint: Ages the watched crops grew by themselves. Bone meal and harvests don't count. Once they have grown %s, a model can be checked against them.
residual.forecaster.made_hint: Eighths of items the watched machines made at their own pace. Once they have made %s, a model can be checked against them.
residual.forecaster.fit_title: The model expects %s of the growth the crops showed
residual.forecaster.fit_title_machines: The model expects %s of the progress the machines showed
residual.forecaster.fit_hint: Within 11%% it runs them four looks for every one; within 25%%, two. Any further off and it is refused: a forecast that can't be trusted runs nothing ahead.
residual.forecaster.state.peeks: This model reads ahead, so it can't forecast.

residual.forecaster.state.refused: Refused: its forecasts are too far off.

fml.menu.mods.info.description.residual:
Rediscover the lost art of building intelligence from scratch.

Someone lived in this world before you, and they seem to have built machines that thought. Find what is left of them, design those machines again from the smallest operations there are, cable them into a real language model, train it on real text with real gradients, and put it to work.
